page: Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-amd is a virtual machine belonging to the High Performance server family, featuring an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor. The configuration includes 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core under a shared CPU allocation model. The processor operates at a base speed of 2.0 GHz and is equipped with 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. It is provisioned with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a 100 GB local NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this server type.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance characteristics and tradeoffs for this shared-resource instance. In stress-ng single-core CPU testing, the server achieves an average score of 2318.46, placing it in the middle 50% of tested systems. However, multi-core performance drops to the bottom 25% with a stress-ng score of 4565.57, reflecting the shared nature of the vCPUs. Memory performance is constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth at 25.27 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 21.3 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 25%. Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations rank in the bottom 10%, indicating that memory-intensive and transactional workloads face throughput limitations.

Given its shared CPU allocation and modest memory capacity, this server type represents a budget-oriented tier. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that do not require sustained, high-throughput compute or memory resources. Appropriate workloads include lightweight web serving, basic development environments, small-scale testing, and simple background tasks. The presence of a 100 GB NVMe SSD provides fast local storage, but the overall system performance profile makes it less suitable for production databases, heavy data processing, or large-scale LLM inference.
